name: Arc VI: Master of Past and Present

pages.name: Arc VI Overview: Master of Past and Present

text.content:
Levels 18–20 · default 10 sessions · expandable to 12. The campaign ends where every earlier question converges: who owns a soul, what Wayreth means by survival, and whether Raistlin can love Caramon without possessing him.

Do not reduce the finale to “stop Raistlin from becoming evil.” By Arc VI the party may sincerely trust him, fear him, owe him lives, disagree with him, admire him, or all five at once. The final arc must honour that complexity.

Default Structure

SessionsMovementPurpose
1Fistandantilus speaksReveal the architect and the interception of Caramon
2Wayreth’s ConfessionReveal the Tower’s survival blind spot
3–4Siege of Two TowersForce strategic choices; Level 19
5Caramon’s WillGive Caramon explicit agency immediately before the Abyss
6Into the AbyssCross the Portal
7Field of Lost NamesIdentity and memory
8Palace of ChainsDestroy or preserve Dominion engine
9Past and PresentRaistlin / Fistandantilus confrontation
10Queen of DarknessFinal battle, decision, ending; Level 20

Sessions 11–12 are optional epilogue sessions: one for immediate aftermath and one for political/magical settlement of the Orders, Towers, Returned and Caramon.

The tracker board determines what arguments, doors and options are available. It does not choose the ending for the players.

TrackerHigh ValueLow Value
Raistlin TrustRaistlin reveals plans, accepts private challenge, gives party time before irreversible acts.He compartmentalises, sets contingencies and assumes interference.
Raistlin ControlHe sees domination as safety and may defend Dominion.He has evidence that consent can survive crisis and seeks alternatives.
Fistandantilus InfluenceThe Dark One’s language feels familiar and persuasive to Raistlin.Raistlin recognises the philosophy as someone else’s pattern sooner.
White Robe BondAt +6 he listens in the Abyss; at +9 he asks before the worst act.He sees the White Robe as Par-Salian’s successor rather than an independent moral authority.
Wayreth AccordAt +5 doors open; at +8 the Tower may act against a direct instruction to preserve a freer future.Wayreth treats the party as external agents and obeys its Master.
War StateHigh values make every delay costly and increase Takhisis’s leverage.Low values give the party more freedom to reject emergency logic.

Rule

Never say “your tracker is too low, so Raistlin ignores you.” Instead, show why he does not trust that argument yet and give the players a final chance to earn a change through action.

The Abyss is not another underground complex. It is a hostile metaphysical environment that turns the campaign’s themes into geography.

Three Laws

  1. Names are anchors. A creature whose true identity is lost becomes easier for the plane to reshape.
  2. Promises have weight. Spoken bargains can become chains, doors or wounds.
  3. Memory is terrain. Places can be built from grief, love, debt or fear and change when those memories are challenged.

Using the Three Components

ArtifactAbyss Use
Heart of MemoryRestores identity erased or distorted by the plane
Chronicle of the Unbroken HourKeeps the party connected to one another across temporal breaks
Bell of True NamesCalls a lost soul back to itself; breaks false identities and ownership claims

Failure Without Dead Ends

A failed scene should cost memory, time, a promise, an ally, position or tracker leverage—not simply make the next door impossible. The finale must keep moving.

Wayreth does not become a talking castle with ordinary emotions. Its confession is delivered through future projections, ward logic and responses to the White Robe.

What the Tower Admits

It examined possible futures as war, dragons and magical catastrophe threatened the Orders. Raistlin appeared in more survival futures than any other viable Master. It therefore chose him.

What It Cannot Understand

The Tower’s core objective is continuation of High Sorcery. It cannot inherently distinguish:

High Sorcery surviving freely.

from

High Sorcery surviving under the absolute domination of a single immortal Master.

Both satisfy survival.

The White Robe’s Role

The White Robe is not asked to replace Raistlin merely because they are White. They are asked whether survival is an adequate objective when freedom, consent and responsibility are part of what makes the institution worth preserving.

High Accord

At Wayreth Accord +8, the party has provided the Tower with enough experiential evidence to recognise a new variable: preservation of autonomous practitioners. That lets it disobey a future order that would preserve magic only through total control.

Everyone enters the final arc wanting something different. None should collapse into a single “good side” or “evil side.”

NPC / ForceWantsWill Not Freely Accept
RaistlinCaramon safe, Takhisis defeated, High Sorcery preserved, no future loss beyond his control.Being powerless again.
CaramonTo decide whether to live, to love his brother without being owned, to stop Raistlin from destroying himself.Being used as proof that Dominion is justified.
FistandantilusRaistlin to complete his philosophy voluntarily and thereby vindicate him.The idea that anything valuable can be allowed to leave.
TakhisisPortal control, destruction/submission of both Towers, removal of rival claim to death and Abyssal power.A mortal redefining the limits of divine authority.
WayrethHigh Sorcery survives.Extinction of the Art.
White Robe PCPlayer-defined by now.Do not prescribe this. The campaign is testing their philosophy too.

Use these to make the plane react to the campaign history rather than generating unrelated fiend encounters.

d12Manifestation
1A road sign points toward a PC's childhood home and the Palace of Chains in the same direction.
2A dead NPC asks the party to remember one detail everyone has forgotten.
3A spoken promise appears as a chain around the speaker's wrist until fulfilled or renounced.
4The moons of Krynn appear for one minute, all at low sanction, then vanish.
5Caramon hears Raistlin's childhood voice rather than the adult one.
6A mirror shows the Black Peace ending as a prosperous city with no visible prisons.
7A name carved into stone is one of the party's old Ispin-adventure NPCs.
8The Heart of Memory grows warm near a lie someone believes about themselves.
9The Chronicle shows a route that takes an hour but costs one remembered day.
10The Bell rings without being touched when a bound soul says “no.”
11Wayreth's bells sound impossibly far away, indicating the mortal link still holds.
12A field of black grass bends toward Raistlin as though he already rules it.

Use this before Session 10 so every major campaign system has an explicit place in the ending.

SystemQuestion at FinalePossible Consequence
CaramonIs his refusal genuinely possible?Remains, departs, or lives independently.
ReturnedWas Dominion removed/redesigned?Free restored community, unstable lives, or controlled military caste.
Black HostWere relationships contracts or ownership?Allies depart, pacts continue, or bound army remains.
WayrethDid survival gain an autonomy criterion?Supports Raistlin, checks him, or chooses new governance.
Palanthas TowerWho controls the Portal?Reopened Lore-spire, sealed Doom-spire, Raistlin's private Tower, or severed Portal.
White RobesDid they learn from their treatment of Raistlin?Reform, backlash, or renewed orthodoxy.
War StateHow much of Ansalon was saved before the finale?Changes political cost and reconstruction.
FistandantilusWas his philosophy actually rejected?Destroyed, trapped, inherited, or left as a surviving idea.

Session 1 · Level 18 · 4 hours. Reveal that the Dark One deliberately arranged the research trail and intercepted Caramon’s displaced soul.

Opening Image

The first direct manifestation occurs in a place Raistlin believes secure: his Palanthas laboratory. A reflection in the Portal continues moving after everyone else stops.

People in Play

  • Fistandantilus
  • Raistlin
  • Caramon
  • Party
  • White Robe PC

Session Sequence

1. The Manifestation

Fistandantilus does not possess Raistlin. He appears as an independent intelligence using the Portal, old wards and accumulated ritual connections.

2. The Claim

He states that the clues were positioned, the fragments preserved, the prophecy cultivated. Raistlin’s research was not accidental.

3. Caramon Revealed

He admits he found Caramon’s displaced soul after Silvanesti and prevented it from returning to the normal flow of death, knowing Raistlin would follow.

4. The Offer

He does not ask Raistlin to surrender his body. He asks him to finish the work and prove that loss itself can be defeated by possession.

5. Break

Raistlin attacks the manifestation or seals the Portal, but cannot erase what was said.

What Can Be Learned

  • Fistandantilus has been an active architect across centuries.
  • Caramon’s unreachable state was engineered after the original catastrophe.
  • The Dark One wants voluntary philosophical succession, not crude possession.

Tracker Guidance

Fistandantilus Influence now becomes active in dialogue. High Influence makes his language feel like conclusions Raistlin already reached; low Influence lets Raistlin recognise the manipulation faster. Trust +1 if the party tells Raistlin the manipulation does not erase his responsibility or grief.

End Beat

Caramon asks the party to meet him without Raistlin present.

Narrative Thread

The reveal does not absolve Raistlin. Fistandantilus manipulated the road, but every step after discovery still involved choices.

Session 2 · Level 18 · 4 hours. Reveal why Wayreth chose Raistlin and give the party a mechanism for changing the Tower’s definition of survival.

Opening Image

The doorway from Palanthas opens into Wayreth without crossing the miles between them. The Tower has never done this for the party before.

People in Play

  • Wayreth intelligence/wards
  • White Robe PC
  • Party
  • Par-Salian optional

Session Sequence

1. The Archive of Futures

Show thousands of rapidly changing projections: Towers destroyed, Orders fractured, dragons triumphant, High Sorcery erased.

2. Raistlin Recurs

In a small but significant subset, High Sorcery survives. Raistlin appears more often than any other Master candidate.

3. The Blind Spot

Show two futures the Tower scores equally: a free Conclave surviving and an immortal Raistlin ruling every wizard. Both preserve High Sorcery.

4. The White Robe’s Question

Ask what the Tower failed to measure. Let the player define the missing principle in their own words.

5. Accord Test

At high Accord, the Tower integrates the new criterion. At lower Accord, it records the argument but cannot yet elevate it over existing Master authority.

What Can Be Learned

  • Wayreth chose survival probability, not goodness.
  • The Tower cannot make moral judgments unless those values become operational criteria.
  • Raistlin’s appointment was not a secret coup or simple corruption.

Tracker Guidance

Wayreth Accord +2 for a concrete, operational answer to what preservation should mean. White Robe Bond may rise later when Raistlin learns what the White Robe told his Tower.

End Beat

The future archive abruptly goes black. Two red points remain: Wayreth and Palanthas, both under attack.

Narrative Thread

This is the philosophical counterpart to the Garden Incident. The party now understands the Tower’s choice well enough to challenge it.

pages.name: Session 3: The Siege of Two Towers I

text.content:
Session 3 · Level 18 · 5 hours. Begin simultaneous assaults and force the party to allocate people, artifacts and magical resources.

Opening Image

Every sending crystal activates at once. Wayreth reports multiple Forest breaches. Palanthas reports dragons over the harbour and cult activity near the Shoikan district.

People in Play

  • Raistlin
  • Caramon
  • Par-Salian/Justarius/Ladonna
  • Palanthas command
  • Wayreth defenders
  • Takhisis forces

Session Sequence

1. Two Maps

Physically present both crisis maps/abstract tracks. The party cannot personally occupy both Towers at once without spending rare movement resources.

2. Allocate Assets

Black Host, Returned volunteers, Knights, Order mages, party allies and named NPCs must be assigned.

3. Wayreth Objective

Prevent enemy magical teams from forcing a permanent contact point into the Forest.

4. Palanthas Objective

Prevent cultists/Dragonarmy agents reaching the Portal support levels while dragons attack conventional defences.

5. Raistlin’s Proposal

He offers to use the Portal to move forces instantly, but doing so opens a larger Abyssal aperture during battle.

What Can Be Learned

  • Takhisis understands both Towers are parts of one strategic system.
  • The party’s earlier allies materially affect available resources.
  • Every extreme shortcut strengthens the Portal’s connection to the Abyss.

Tracker Guidance

War State ±1 from each theatre’s outcome. Control ±1 if party chooses or rejects coercive shortcuts; Trust responds to competence and honesty rather than agreement.

End Beat

Whichever theatre received fewer resources suffers a breach that becomes Session 5’s primary crisis.

Narrative Thread

The finale forces choices with opportunity cost. The party cannot save everything by simply being high level.

pages.name: Session 4: The Siege of Two Towers II

text.content:
Session 4 · Level 19 · 5 hours. Resolve the simultaneous siege, elevate the party to Level 19, and make the cost of delaying the Abyss expedition clear.

Opening Image

Smoke, magical darkness and moving forest paths make both battles feel unlike ordinary sieges. The party arrives at the crisis they could not prevent in Session 4.

People in Play

  • Theatre-specific allies
  • Takhisis elite commander
  • Raistlin
  • Caramon
  • Wayreth/Palanthas Tower systems

Session Sequence

1. Breach

Use the weaker theatre from prior allocation: Wayreth archive incursion or Palanthas lower-seal penetration.

2. Tower Choice

At high Accord, Wayreth may disobey a destructive defensive order to preserve autonomous allies. At low Accord, Raistlin must explicitly countermand it.

3. Portal Surge

Takhisis briefly reaches through the larger aperture. Her presence is felt before her avatar is seen.

4. Strategic Victory

The party closes mortal-world attacks but learns the assaults will repeat while Takhisis can pressure the Portal from the other side.

5. Decision

Raistlin concludes the war cannot be won defensively. They must enter the Abyss and destroy the dominion machinery/Fistandantilus threat at its source.

What Can Be Learned

  • Takhisis can use Portal instability to project force.
  • Neither Tower can remain in permanent siege indefinitely.
  • The next phase must be offensive and planar.

Tracker Guidance

Level 19. War State stabilises based on victory. Wayreth Accord pays off here; if low, let the party earn one last increase through saving Tower inhabitants rather than merely walls.

End Beat

Raistlin opens the Portal fully enough to show a horizon that cannot exist beneath any sky on Krynn.

Narrative Thread

The mortal war is temporarily held. The campaign leaves Krynn to decide what kind of victory will return.

Session 5 · Level 18 · 3–4 hours. Give Caramon a private voice independent of both Raistlin and Fistandantilus before the final strategic crisis.

Opening Image

Caramon chooses somewhere ordinary for the conversation if possible: kitchen, quiet inn room, training yard. He does not want to discuss his soul in a laboratory.

People in Play

  • Caramon
  • Party
  • Optional one trusted family/friend echo or survivor

Session Sequence

1. What He Remembers

He remembers Silvanesti, death, fragments of being called, and waking. He does not remember Fistandantilus’s captivity as coherent time.

2. The Question

He tells the party: “I don’t know whether I came back because I wanted to.” Let the silence work.

3. What He Wants

Caramon may want to live, may be uncertain, or may ultimately want release. Let this be shaped by how the players have treated him, not a fixed answer. His non-negotiable demand is the ability to choose.

4. The Ask

He asks the party to make Raistlin hear him without turning the brothers into enemies if that can be avoided.

What Can Be Learned

  • Caramon loves Raistlin.
  • He does not equate love with consent to the ritual.
  • He is prepared to oppose Dominion but not automatically prepared to die.

Tracker Guidance

White Robe Bond can rise if the PC listens to Caramon rather than using him as moral evidence. Raistlin Control may later fall if the party carries Caramon’s wishes accurately.

End Beat

Before the conversation ends, Wayreth sends an impossible message: a door appears in the wall where there was none, opening onto its deepest archive.

Narrative Thread

Caramon is not the campaign’s moral prop. This session gives the player group a person whose wishes may complicate every preferred ending.

Session 6 · Level 19 · 4 hours. Cross the Portal, establish Abyssal laws, and separate the party from ordinary logistical support.

Opening Image

The Portal opens like a wound becoming a doorway. On the other side is a plain under a sky with no moon. Names spoken aloud echo for too long.

People in Play

  • Raistlin
  • Party
  • Caramon optional but strongly recommended
  • Abyssal guide/contact if Black Host relations good

Session Sequence

1. Last Preparations

Choose what comes through. Each component/artifact matters. Contacts may provide safe first steps if prior agreements were honoured.

2. Crossing

Every character must state their own name. The plane reacts differently to names spoken willingly versus titles imposed by others.

3. Cut the Line

Once across, ordinary sending to Krynn is unreliable. The Chronicle preserves the party’s temporal link back.

4. First Threat

A soul-storm attempts to strip memories/names rather than deal ordinary damage.

What Can Be Learned

  • Identity has metaphysical weight in the Abyss.
  • The three Long Return artifacts function as survival tools, not only ritual components.
  • Fistandantilus’s dominion system is embedded deeper in the plane.

Tracker Guidance

Trust +1 if Raistlin allows shared operational command. Control shifts if he insists Caramon remain or go against Caramon’s stated choice.

End Beat

A road appears made from engraved names, most of them crossed out.

Narrative Thread

The Abyss literalises the campaign: names, memories, promises and ownership become physical systems.

pages.name: Session 7: The Field of Lost Names

text.content:
Session 7 · Level 19 · 4–5 hours. Use the Bell of True Names to rescue identity and show the scale of souls affected by Abyssal power.

Opening Image

Thousands of figures wander a colourless field. They respond to descriptions of who they were but not to names they no longer remember.

People in Play

  • Lost souls
  • A soul the party recognises from earlier campaign events
  • Abyssal name-thief
  • Raistlin/Caramon

Session Sequence

1. Recognition

The party sees at least one dead NPC from an earlier arc. Do not promise resurrection; simply let recognition matter.

2. Name-Thief

An entity hoards stolen names as objects. Defeating it by destruction risks scattering them permanently.

3. Use the Bell

The Bell can call individual true names back to their owners. Each ringing attracts attention from deeper powers.

4. Caramon Echo

If Caramon accompanies the party, the field tries to split “Caramon as Raistlin remembers him” from Caramon’s current self. The Heart of Memory repairs the distinction.

What Can Be Learned

  • A soul can be damaged by losing identity without being destroyed.
  • The Bell restores recognition without issuing commands.
  • Raistlin sees a working model of power that restores without possession.

Tracker Guidance

Control -1–2 if the party/raistlin use the Bell to restore rather than claim names. Fistandantilus Influence falls 1 if Raistlin explicitly recognises that restoration did not require ownership.

End Beat

The freed names form a path to a palace whose towers are made from chains.

Narrative Thread

This session supplies evidence for an alternative philosophy: power can return something to itself rather than to the caster.

Session 8 · Level 19 · 5 hours. Confront the physical mechanism behind Dominion resurrection and decide whether to destroy, seize or redesign it.

Opening Image

Every chain in the palace is attached to something invisible. Touching one produces a memory: a promise made under duress, a debt, a true name, a dead person being told to return.

People in Play

  • Dominion engine
  • Bound souls
  • Fistandantilus projections
  • Raistlin
  • Caramon

Session Sequence

1. Map the Mechanism

The engine converts emotional/temporal anchors into ownership channels. The Long Return’s command flaw originates here.

2. Useful Power

Destroying it immediately will also sever several protections currently keeping Returned stable on Krynn. This prevents a trivial moral choice.

3. Redesign Option

With sufficient research and party creativity, the engine can be altered so anchors maintain connection without command authority. It is difficult and may require temporary sacrifice.

4. Raistlin’s Choice

High Control Raistlin argues to seize it until the war ends. Low Control/Bond Raistlin accepts destruction/redesign. Middling values produce a genuine argument.

5. Break the Chains

Resolve combat/puzzle against the engine’s guardians while the philosophical choice is implemented.

What Can Be Learned

  • Dominion is a separate layer imposed on restoration.
  • The Returned can potentially survive without obedience if the engine is redesigned.
  • Fistandantilus built metaphysical possession into his system deliberately.

Tracker Guidance

Control can move ±3. White Robe Bond +1–2 if the PC offers a technically credible alternative. Fistandantilus Influence falls if his machinery is rejected in principle, even if temporarily preserved for lives.

End Beat

When the central chain breaks or changes, a door opens and Fistandantilus stands beyond it in person—or as close to person as he can be here.

Narrative Thread

This is the last mechanical argument. Session 9 is personal.

Session 9 · Level 19 · 5 hours. Stage the direct Raistlin–Fistandantilus confrontation and force the philosophy of possession into explicit language.

Opening Image

Fistandantilus greets Raistlin not as a victim or apprentice but as a colleague who has finally arrived late to his own conclusion.

People in Play

  • Fistandantilus
  • Raistlin
  • Caramon
  • White Robe PC
  • Party

Session Sequence

1. No Possession

Fistandantilus explicitly rejects crude body theft as unnecessary. He wants Raistlin to choose the work.

2. The Offer

Caramon permanently restored. Dead companions returned. Takhisis defeated. Orders protected. Portal controlled. No future loss that Raistlin does not permit.

3. The Price

Nothing he loves will ever again be allowed to leave him.

4. Caramon Answers

Caramon speaks for himself. His answer depends on Session 2 and the condition of the command channel.

5. Party Argument

Use trackers as openness, not outcome. At White Bond +6 Raistlin genuinely listens. At +9 he asks the White Robe what they would do before deciding.

6. Break with the Dark One—or Accept

Raistlin’s decision can be provisional; Takhisis interrupts before a clean philosophical ending.

What Can Be Learned

  • Fistandantilus’s core belief is that value creates a right to possession.
  • Raistlin’s grief has approached the same conclusion but does not have to finish there.
  • Caramon’s independent will is the factual test of the philosophy.

Tracker Guidance

This session can move Trust, Control, Influence and White Bond by large final amounts if player actions justify it. Do not let numbers substitute for scene quality.

End Beat

The Abyss shakes. Takhisis arrives before the argument can become private again.

Narrative Thread

Everything in the campaign has prepared the party to speak here with evidence: roads saved, Returned met, souls called, Towers defended, and Caramon himself present.

Session 10 · Level 20 · 5–6 hours. Resolve Takhisis, Fistandantilus, the Portal and Raistlin’s final decision without erasing the consequences of earlier choices.

Opening Image

The final battlefield is not a throne room. It is the collapsing intersection of the Portal, the Palace of Chains, Caramon’s soul-anchor and the paths back to Krynn.

People in Play

  • Takhisis avatar
  • Raistlin
  • Fistandantilus
  • Caramon
  • Party
  • Abyssal allies/enemies based on Black Host choices

Session Sequence

1. Takhisis’s Claim

She names both wizards thieves attempting to seize powers belonging to gods. She attacks the bonds holding the party together, not just hit points.

2. Three Fronts

Run simultaneous objectives: survive/defeat avatar, stop Fistandantilus taking the Dominion system, stabilise the Portal/Caramon link.

3. Raistlin’s Decision

Depending on relationship and player persuasion, he may release Caramon, share authority, seize the system, sacrifice himself, or attempt transcendence.

4. Fistandantilus End

The Dark One is destroyed, trapped, absorbed, released to oblivion, or denied succession. Do not let him escape merely to preserve a sequel unless players create that outcome.

5. Close or Transform the Portal

Determine what happens to the Returned, Black Host contracts and both Towers.

6. Return

The party crosses back to Krynn—or some do not—into a world whose war state reflects the campaign they actually played.

What Can Be Learned

  • The final answer belongs to the party, not to a preselected canon ending.
  • Caramon chooses his own fate if free enough to do so.
  • Wayreth’s future depends on both survival and whatever principle the party taught it.

Tracker Guidance

Level 20 at resolution. Use final tracker values to describe consequences and relationships, not to award “good” or “bad” points.

End Beat

Choose the ending family that follows from play, then give every PC an individual epilogue question: What did power cost you, and what did you refuse to let it take?

Narrative Thread

The campaign began with a funeral and a road to a Tower. It ends with the party deciding whether love, magic and survival require ownership—or whether the greatest act of power is sometimes to let another person choose.

Use these as consequence frameworks, not locked scripts. Mix elements when play demands it.

The Black Mage Remains

Raistlin releases Caramon, destroys Dominion, defeats Takhisis and remains Black Robe Master of Wayreth/Palanthas: dangerous, proud and no longer willing to enslave the dead.

White and Black

Raistlin and the White Robe become mutual counterweights in a reformed Orders system where forbidden research is judged by consent, consequence and responsibility rather than colour alone.

The Black Peace

The party supports Raistlin’s control. He masters Returned and Black Host, defeats Takhisis, ends the war and creates peace in which death itself answers to him.

The Last Sacrifice

Raistlin releases Caramon, traps himself with Fistandantilus and greater Abyssal powers beyond the Portal, and closes it. Wayreth’s bells ring; the Master’s chamber opens to another.

Master of Past and Present

Raistlin refuses all restraint, destroys Fistandantilus, defeats Takhisis, takes Abyssal power and transcends mortality. The last confrontation becomes the PCs against the man they helped reach this point.

Epilogue Questions

  • What becomes of the Returned?
  • What legal/political status does the Black Host agreement leave behind?
  • Who controls the Tower of Palanthas?
  • Does Wayreth still recognise Raistlin as Master?
  • What do the three Orders change because of the White Robe’s example?
  • Does Caramon remain, depart, or build a life independent of his brother?
  • Which place from Arc I is finally at peace—and which never recovers?
